claims.title: How many points of one torus fibre are fixed?
claims.hypotheses: The fibre is a complex torus with a full period lattice preserved by its linear action. The first leg is injective on the fibre and 1 is not a fibre eigenvalue.
claims.statement: The coincidence points form a finite group of order |detℂ(I−Θ)|².

claims.title: What distinguishes a point count from a trace on the square elliptic curve?
claims.hypotheses: The square elliptic curve has multiplier 4 or 4i and the first leg is the identity.
claims.statement: The nine points for multiplier 4 have total graded trace 12y−3. The seventeen points for multiplier 4i give (1+4i)(1−4iy).

claims.title: What is the trace contribution of a whole fibre?
claims.hypotheses: The two legs form a smooth proper correspondence with transverse coincidences and first leg étale. The vertical action is Θ and the base action is T.
claims.statement: The sum of the local graded holomorphic traces in one fibre is D_T(y)D_Θ(y) conjugate(D_Θ(1))/D_T(1).

claims.title: How can finitely many integral labels select a weight?

claims.statement: One finite complex linear combination of products of determinants at nonzero even integral labels gives the full product of Schur polynomials, universally in the root lists.
